_note: Shared lessons as data: what one game found that another game will need, when no card or doc has room for it or it fits none. A lesson in games/<game>.md is tagged `[kb <id>]` (docs/LEARNING.md 3) and the entry is written here in the same change. No size budget: nobody reads this file end to end. `python tools/knowledge.py lessons WORD ...` searches it and every game's own lessons; `lessons --game GAME` lists the entries that apply. Fields: `id` lesson.<name> (unique); `title`; `text` (the lesson, with its limit); `level` observed | inferred | demonstrated; `sources` (games/<game>.md files that found it: add a game when it meets the lesson again); `words` (search terms a new game would use); optional `when` (predicates of docs/techniques/predicates.json: the entry applies unless one is known false; empty = every game) and `card` (the card it belongs with, to fold in when that card is next revised). tools/knowledge.py check validates the structure, never the truth.

lessons.title: NEXLOAD overwrites the printer buffer before the game starts
lessons.text: NEXLOAD leaves its own data in 0x5B00-0x5BFF. A snapshot that keeps its stack, code or a flag there (128K: the ROM paging code at 0x5B00 and BANKM 0x5B5C) starts wrong unless the build restores it: `keep_printer_buffer` in the converter, or a set-up call in the stub. Restore the whole 256 bytes, not only the start-up tail, and do not widen an allocation proved for part of the buffer. Boot every build with nexload=True before calling its start safe. Limit: a read of 0x5B5C alone did not matter in Atom Ant or Ruff and Reddy (real loader, every mode); check what the game does with the byte. See BRIEFING C2 #36, #38.

lessons.title: A JNext memory dump is physical SRAM, not CPU memory
lessons.text: JNext's mem/ram.bin has a 0x40000 physical offset before ordinary Next RAM, and bank 5 is dedicated video RAM. Rebuild what the CPU sees through the MMU registers, never from raw file offsets. Assert a known signature (the hook code) before reading state from a page: an all-zero count at every checkpoint was the wrong offset, not an empty table.

lessons.title: JNext drops key presses made before the .nex has loaded
lessons.text: Loading a .nex in JNext clears earlier key presses. Schedule a run's keys after the load and confirm from the game's own state that they arrived; otherwise a run labelled moving or firing measured a neutral-input game.

lessons.title: Copy results out of a pooled simulator before the slot is reused
lessons.text: A simulator from simpool.machine is reused by the next call on the same slot. Keeping a reference to it instead of copying the result registers and memory made two different outcomes compare equal.

lessons.title: The plain .nex is not the pace control for a game that beeps through the ROM
lessons.text: The plain .nex runs NextZXOS's ROM3, whose BEEP ran 12% faster than Sinclair's in JNext. A game that makes sound through the ROM needs the original .z80 on a 48K machine as its pace control.

lessons.title: A pace window's own overhead at 28 MHz is multiplied by K
lessons.text: The time a pace window spends on itself at 28 MHz is scaled by K like everything else in it. Account it as debt, or the target grows with every window.

lessons.title: Check what a limiter can repay against the worst update, and read the debt's clamp first
lessons.text: A limiter that only waits cannot repay a debt larger than its window (Nightshade: 240 lines of blit against 560 of hooks). When a pace table shows a slow stretch, look at the debt's clamp before anything else: Atic Atac's clamp of -192 lines threw away most of what room changes cost, and read as 'the limiter cannot repay'.

lessons.title: Catch-up credit must be measurable, and is worth more at 28 MHz than its line count
lessons.text: Credit a catch-up gap by line count only when the gap is under a frame, and end it before any longer stretch. Run the catch-up clock as low as the build allows: at 28 MHz a gap's real gain was 3 to 8 times its lines (hooks in it against contended writes), at 7 MHz near 2 whatever it holds, so a fixed credit stays honest only there.

lessons.title: One floor per update cannot pace a game whose displaced work varies by figure
lessons.text: A single floor reads slow where the original is light and fast where it is busy, and the whole-run figure hides both. Windows on what was displaced, sized from the plain build, held nearly every stretch within 2%. A window that reads line and frame serial needs the two in step at the wrap (a mismatch read as 164 lines of false time per interrupt); a window under a frame needs only the wrap.
